chunks: And from him (Al-Hadi) from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'When a man intends divorce, he divorces her before the end of her waiting period without sexual intercourse. Indeed, if he divorces her once and leaves her until her waiting period expires or after it, she is considered with him as having one divorce. If he divorces her a second time and wishes to propose to her while the suitor is present, provided he left her until her waiting period expired, or if he wishes to take her back before the waiting period ends, and if he does so, she is with him as having two divorces. If he divorces her three times, then she is not permissible to him... until she marries another husband.' And she inherits and is inherited from as long as she remains in the first two divorces.

As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Shu'ayb al-Haddad from Ma'alla ibn Khunays from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): From a man who divorced his wife, then did not take her back until she had three menstrual periods, then married her, then divorced her, and left her until she had three menstrual periods, then married her, then divorced her, and left her until she had three menstrual periods, without taking her back (meaning having sexual intercourse with her). He said: 'He may marry her forever as long as he does not take her back and have sexual intercourse.'

His saying (peace be upon him): 'He may marry her forever as long as he does not take her back and have sexual intercourse' implies that the meaning is if she had married another husband and then separated from him by death or divorce, because in any case where the matter is as we described, it is permissible for him to marry her forever, because the husband destroys the first divorce. And in the report it is not stated that it is permissible for him to marry her if she did not marry another husband. And if that is not apparent in its text, we interpret it as we mentioned. And that which indicates that the husband's entry (consummation) is considered in what we mentioned is what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between triple divorce and the requirement of a new marriage in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shia juristic distinction between *raj'i* (revocable) and *ba'in* (irrevocable) divorces, emphasizing that the husband's right to remarry without a new contract depends on whether the intermediate marriage was consummated. It highlights the scholarly nuance that mere contractual marriage (*nikah*) without sexual intercourse (*dakhil*) does not break the bond of the first divorce, whereas consummation establishes a full marital bond requiring a new contract for re-marriage. This ruling underscores the practical importance of *iddah* and consummation in determining the status of the wife during the waiting period.
